newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Room occupancy dips, rates rise in NZ hotel survey.
newsitem.headline: Room occupancy dips, rates rise in NZ hotel survey.

text.p: Average room occupancies fell 0.9 percentage points to 68.1 percent in the Ernst and Young 1995/96 New Zealand hotel survey, but average achieved room rates rose 3.7 percent to NZ$119.12.
Average house profit remained static at 27.3 percent of total revenue, while Auckland and Rotorua hotels achieved the greatest improvements in profitability of the main centres.
Christchurch and Queenstown hotels suffered the most significant falls in profitability.

Ernst and Young said Christchurch, Queenstown and Rotorua hotel markets would be over-supplied with rooms for the next 18-24 months unless there was a substantial growth in international visitor nights during the period.
Supply of serviced apartments had also seen substantial growth, especially in Auckland and Christchurch but also in Queenstown.

New Zealand Tourism Industry Association Chairman Graeme McDowell said that for a number of regions, growth in supply of new rooms had greatly exceeded demand. The rise of the New Zealand dollar had been a major contributor to a slow-down in
demand, especially from mature markets, but in some regions the high growth in supply of rooms was a greater factor.
